note: While SNUPN deficiency predominantly causes early restrictive respiratory failure, a recent case report documents primary myocardial damage, challenging the claim that cardiopulmonary dysfunction is exclusively respiratory.

evidence.text: A case report describes limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R29 presenting with myocardial damage as the initial clinical manifestation, suggesting primary cardiac muscle involvement can occur.

source.title: A Case of Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type R29 Presenting with Myocardial Damage as the Initial Manifestation: A case report
source.quote: A Case of Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type R29 Presenting with Myocardial Damage as the Initial Manifestation

numbers.metric: affected individuals reported with initial myocardial damage

evidence.text: Adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy cases consistently present with prominent proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness alongside early restrictive respiratory impairment.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement.
